name: Jena Nelson
bio: Jena Nelson taught in Oklahoma schools for more than 16 years and was named Oklahoma Teacher of the Year in 2020. She was the Democratic nominee for Oklahoma Superintendent of Public Instruction in 2022 and has since worked in nonprofit development, including as acting executive director of the Oklahoma Faith Network. She is the Democratic nominee for Oklahoma's 5th congressional district.

platform.point: Protect Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid through drug price negotiation, fraud reduction and more preventive care.
Ease costs for working families with price caps on essentials, expanded food assistance, housing relief and worker protections.
Keep the border secure while reforming the asylum system and widening legal work pathways.
Improve VA health and mental health services and oppose cuts to veterans' programs.

economy.evidence: Calls for price caps on essentials and worker protections and opposes tax breaks for the wealthiest.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect and strengthen Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid and expand food assistance.

immigration.evidence: Pairs border enforcement with asylum reform and more legal work pathways.

education.evidence: Wants free school meals for all Oklahoma public school children.

notes: The education score rests on her school-meals pledge; her issues page does not address vouchers.

name: Robert P. Henri
bio: Robert Patrick Henri is an independent candidate for Oklahoma's 5th congressional district. His campaign, Project Due Course, centres on congressional ethics and process reforms.

platform.point: Enact term limits for members of Congress.
Ban members of Congress from trading individual stocks.
Adopt an enforceable Supreme Court ethics code with outside oversight and penalties.
Require a waiting period before votes so bills can be read, longer for bigger bills.
Have independent commissions draw congressional district lines.
Require the Department of Defense to pass a full financial audit.

notes: Listed on the state candidate list as Robert P. Henri; his platform addresses government-ethics reforms that do not map onto the scored domains.

name: Austin Nieves
bio: Austin Nieves is an entertainer and dancer running as an independent for Oklahoma's 5th congressional district.
notes: No campaign website or published issue positions were found; occupation comes from the Wikipedia election page.

name: Suzanne Bonamici
bio: Suzanne Bonamici has represented Oregon's 1st congressional district since 2012, after serving in the Oregon House and Oregon Senate. Before elected office she was a consumer protection attorney, including at the Federal Trade Commission and Legal Aid. She serves on the Education and the Workforce Committee and the Science, Space and Technology Committee.

platform.point: Work toward universal coverage while protecting the Affordable Care Act and lowering prescription drug costs.
Take action on the climate crisis and protect the environment.
Advocate for strong public education.
Expand economic opportunity and address the needs of working families.
Protect abortion rights and civil rights.
Take steps to protect democratic institutions.

economy.evidence: Has backed ending tax cuts for the highest earners and favored stimulus over market-led recovery.

welfare.evidence: Member of the Medicare for All Caucus and supports universal health coverage.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion access, universal background checks and limits on large-capacity magazines.

security.evidence: Supports police accountability measures and reduced incarceration.

immigration.evidence: Supports a pathway to citizenship for undocumented immigrants and the DREAM Act.

foreign.evidence: Voted to support Israel after the October 7 attacks and backs multilateral institutions.

energy.evidence: Backs the Green New Deal and a clean-electricity target, and served on the Select Committee on the Climate Crisis.

education.evidence: Opposes school vouchers and calls public education central to communities and the economy.

faith.evidence: Member of the Congressional Freethought Caucus, which promotes secular government.

name: Barbara Kahl
bio: Barbara Kahl is a veterinarian who has practised in Oregon for more than 30 years. Her campaign says her family has lived in northwest Oregon for about a century. She is the Republican nominee for Oregon's 1st congressional district.

platform.point: Support small businesses and infrastructure investment to create jobs.
Strengthen public schools while expanding school choice and vocational paths, with funding that follows the student.
Increase housing supply by streamlining permits and reducing financing barriers for first-time buyers.
Fund local law enforcement and hold it accountable.
Manage forests and land in ways that support timber-dependent communities.
Lower health costs and improve care for veterans and families.

economy.evidence: Emphasises cutting red tape for small businesses alongside infrastructure investment.

security.evidence: Calls for funding local law enforcement paired with accountability.

education.evidence: Backs expanded school choice with student-centered funding while also strengthening public schools.

notes: Wikipedia notes a Log Cabin Republicans endorsement; no campaign social accounts were linked on the site.

name: Cliff Bentz
bio: Cliff Bentz has represented Oregon's 2nd congressional district since 2021, after serving in the Oregon House from 2008 to 2018 and the Oregon Senate from 2018 to 2020. Born in Salem and raised on eastern Oregon ranches, he is an attorney focused on agricultural, water and property law. He also served on the Oregon Water Resources Commission.

platform.point: Stop illegal immigration through stronger border security, including completing the wall.
Lower taxes and reduce regulation to strengthen the rural economy.
Defend water rights for farmers and ranchers and back trade deals such as USMCA.
Hold federal agencies accountable for forest management and reduce wildfire risk.
Streamline hydropower relicensing and protect the Bonneville Power Administration's low-cost power.
Oppose government-run health care in favor of market-based approaches.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on lower taxes and less regulation and voted for the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

welfare.evidence: Opposes government-run health care and voted against the Affordable Insulin Now Act in 2022.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion except to save the mother's life, opposes background checks on private gun sales, and voted against final passage of the Respect for Marriage Act.

security.evidence: Has favored mandatory minimum sentences and keeping existing police accountability rules.

immigration.evidence: Backs a border wall and ICE enforcement and voted for the Laken Riley Act, but supported the Farm Workforce Modernization Act.

foreign.evidence: Supports a strong military and backed Israel after October 7, with a mixed record on Ukraine aid.

energy.evidence: Led legislative walkouts against Oregon cap-and-trade and focuses on preserving existing hydropower.

faith.evidence: Survey answers indicate strong support for religious liberty and for Judeo-Christian values in public life.

notes: The faith score is new and rests on a 2020 survey summarised by OnTheIssues.

name: Chris Beck
bio: Chris Beck represented the 12th district in the Oregon House of Representatives from 1997 to 2003. Born in Portland, he worked in land conservation at the Trust for Public Land and served as a rural policy adviser at the U.S. Department of Agriculture from 2010 to 2016. He holds degrees from Brown University and Harvard's Kennedy School.

platform.point: Repeal HR-1 Medicaid cuts affecting rural hospitals, create a public care option, and draw clinicians to rural areas.
End the Iran war and cancel tariffs to bring down fuel prices.
Offer low-interest financing for rural homebuyers and use federal programs for Main Street development.
Expand conservation programs, create a rural service corps, and support beginning farmers and ranchers.
Fund projects such as a new Crater Lake lodge and artist live-work spaces in rural towns.

economy.evidence: Proposes federal housing financing and development programs and fewer tax breaks for luxury homes.

welfare.evidence: Wants HR-1 Medicaid cuts repealed and a public care option created.

immigration.evidence: Seeks a sensible, bipartisan approach to legal immigration, noting farm workers who have gone into hiding.

foreign.evidence: Calls for ending the Iran war.

notes: The immigration score rests on a brief mention of legal immigration on his issues page.

name: Maxine Dexter
bio: Maxine Dexter has represented Oregon's 3rd congressional district since January 2025, after serving in the Oregon House from 2020 to 2024. A pulmonologist and critical care physician with Kaiser Permanente, she was born in Bothell, Washington, and trained at the University of Washington. She serves on the Natural Resources and Veterans' Affairs committees.

platform.point: Work for universal access to affordable, high-quality health care.
Dismantle ICE and base immigration policy on due process and dignity.
Push for immediate federal climate action and hold fossil fuel companies accountable.
Expand the supply of safe, affordable housing.
Support unions, fair wages and job security.
Defend equal legal protection and safety for LGBTQ+ people.

economy.evidence: Supports stronger employee protections, union rights and more public housing funding.

welfare.evidence: Supports moving to a single-payer health care system.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights, LGBTQ equality and fentanyl test strip decriminalization; favors stricter gun control.

immigration.evidence: Calls for defunding and dismantling ICE and opposes mass deportation.

foreign.evidence: Cosponsored the Block the Bombs Act to restrict offensive weapons transfers to Israel.

energy.evidence: Calls for bold federal climate action, renewable energy build-out and emissions cuts.

name: Loran Ayles
bio: Loran Ayles is a heavy equipment operator and the Republican nominee for Oregon's 3rd congressional district.
notes: No campaign website or published issue positions were found; occupation comes from state filing records cited on Wikipedia.

name: Val Hoyle
bio: Val Hoyle has represented Oregon's 4th congressional district since 2023. She was Oregon Labor Commissioner from 2019 to 2023 and served in the Oregon House from 2009 to 2017, including as majority leader. Born in California and raised in New Hampshire, she moved to Lane County in 1999.

platform.point: Expand union jobs, paid leave and apprenticeships and crack down on wage theft.
Pursue universal health care, protect the Affordable Care Act and rein in drug prices.
Invest in affordable housing, renter tax credits and down-payment help.
Prioritise wildfire prevention and a transition to renewable energy.
Increase K-12 and higher education funding and make community college free.
Curb dark money, overturn Citizens United and protect vote-by-mail.

economy.evidence: Backs paid leave, stronger wage enforcement, drug price regulation and action against anticompetitive practices.

liberty.evidence: As a state legislator backed background checks for most gun sales and medical marijuana outlets (guns, drugs); her campaign defends abortion access (abortion).

security.evidence: As a state legislator supported shorter sentences for non-violent offenses.

immigration.evidence: Opposed increased ICE and CBP funding and voted against final passage of the Laken Riley Act.

foreign.evidence: Member of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, voted to withdraw troops from Syria, and has backed limits on arms to Israel.

energy.evidence: As a state legislator pushed to move Oregon off coal and expand renewable power.

education.evidence: Wants more K-12 and higher education funding and free community college.

notes: An unverified faith score based on Freethought Caucus membership was removed; liberty and security draw partly on her Oregon legislative record. A 2026 endorsement from the Leading the Future AI super PAC was noted, but it does not set a tech score.

name: Monique DeSpain
current_role: Attorney and retired Air Force colonel
bio: Monique DeSpain is a retired U.S. Air Force colonel with more than 30 years of service who has worked as a military and private-sector lawyer. She lives in Eugene and was the Republican nominee for Oregon's 4th congressional district in 2024.

platform.point: Cut taxes and regulations to encourage private-sector job growth and ease inflation.
Secure the border while offering one-time lawful status to long-settled, non-criminal residents who meet strict conditions.
Give police the resources they need and stop fentanyl trafficking.
Restore active forest management through thinning, sustainable harvests and quick fire suppression.
Return decisions to parents with transparency, performance reporting and school choice.
Require photo ID to vote and U.S.-made certified voting machines.

economy.evidence: Calls for cutting taxes and regulations to spur private-sector job creation.

security.evidence: Wants law enforcement given more authority and resources and opposes lenient crime policies.

immigration.evidence: Prioritises border security but backs one-time lawful status for long-settled, non-criminal residents.

foreign.evidence: Supports military readiness, backing Israel and confronting China, with strict oversight of foreign aid.

energy.evidence: Backs an all-of-the-above energy approach without government mandates.

education.evidence: Supports parental decision-making and school choice.

notes: The campaign Facebook page is named on her site but its URL could not be confirmed. No headshot URL was found on the issues page.

name: Justin Filip
bio: Justin Filip is the Pacific Green Party nominee for Oregon's 4th congressional district.
notes: No campaign website, biography or issue positions were found.
